_note: News leads (news/leads.mjs). Only feeds meant for automated reading, each fetched live with the pipeline's own honest user agent and allowed by the site's robots.txt on the date in verified_at. primary: the official body's own releases (a news item may be written from them, quotes and numbers checked by code); secondary: press (never published automatically, reported as leads only). A site that blocks automated readers (403, a bot challenge) is listed under rejected and is never worked around. secondary_paths / secondary_titles mark op-eds on an official site: opinion, not an official release, so those items are leads only. sponsor: the member whose own feed it is (a weak match only: it never sets an item's tracker). secondary_paths are tested on both the feed link and the release link ("In the News" press reposts on house.gov are press). state: the two-letter code of a state body's own feed (a bill number with no state written next to it is read as that state's). type html_teasers: an official listing page read like a feed (only teasers with their own machine-readable date).

sources._note: NIST news. Most CAISI (now CAISSI) posts are 'updates' this feed leaves out: they come from nist-caissi below.

The CAISI page (https://www.nist.gov/caisi redirects here; renamed Center for Advancing Innovation and Standards for Super Intelligence) lists its latest posts as teasers with a machine-readable date (news/feeds.mjs parseTeaserPage). Checked live 28 Oct 2026: 8 teasers, incl. the GLM-5.3 and Kimi K3 assessments and the incident-response key practices, none of them in the NIST news feed; robots.txt allows /caissi. NIST's topic feeds for CAISI, CAISSI and super intelligence are valid but empty.
Already a pipeline source: documents become entries and fixed-wording news through the grabber and Tier A / Tier B, so news/leads.mjs does not read it again.
